title: Terminate watch mode via natural process exit when possible
body:

### Description

It has been a long-standing issue that certain watch-mode tests are a little flaky on CI and do not shut down properly. I took some time now to let my agent run some local stress tests in docker and it managed to not only confirm the flakiness but track it down to an unresolved issue that apparently affects all NodeJS versions and is unlikely to be fixed any time soon: nodejs/node#54918

The problem occurs when we call `process.exit` in response to an external shutdown signal, i.e. Ctrl+C, which is also an issue that actual users are exposed to when leaving watch mode. If `process.exit` coincides with certain internal cleanup processes then it can leave rollup hanging in an unrecoverable state.

The implemented solution is rather simple: Instead of directly exiting we just set the exitCode. This would usually lead to a natural exit once the event loop runs dry that is not affected by the bug.

However, there will not be such an exit if any plugin etc. still has some timers or other IO handles open. So I learned that you can set an unreferenced timeout

```js
setTimeout(() => process.exit(exitCode), 200).unref();
```

which will not prevent a natural exit but will do a force exit if the natural one does not complete within 200ms.

I hope this finally resolves those issues.
